beats.t: Nothing had been going Yeoni’s way lately. One unlucky day would have been easy enough to shrug off, but little things had been going wrong for days.
That morning was no different. There had definitely been three alarms: 7:10, 7:15, and 7:20. Yeoni had even given each one a proper name.
[ Get up ]   [ Seriously, get up ]   [ Keep this up and your life is over ]
Not one had rung. By the time Yeoni opened their eyes, the light slipping through the curtains had turned yellow. Exactly the color of being late.
The phone was at 1 percent. The charger sat neatly in the outlet. The problem was the other end: it wasn’t connected to the phone.
…You cutting me off too?
The charger said nothing. That day, it felt as though everything in the world had quietly turned its back on Yeoni alone.
The sock on the left was white; the one on the right, gray. Even the patterns were different. Yeoni stared down for about three seconds.
…They say mixing and matching is fashionable these days.
Yeoni decided to look on the bright side. Staying positive was the only way they knew to weather bad luck.
The real trouble was the bus. Yeoni tapped the card—beep. Please try again.
Another tap. Beep. Please try again. And another. Beep. Please try again. The people behind Yeoni watched without a word.
(That silence was the worst part.) …You worked fine yesterday.
The card finally registered on the fourth try. By then, the trust between them had already taken a small hit.
(Yeoni left a mental review.) Transit card… one star. Reason: took four tries. Would not buy again.

For lunch, Yeoni bought a tuna-mayo rice triangle. The moment the wrapper came off, it fell face-first onto the floor. Rice scattered everywhere; with half its seaweed peeled away, it looked utterly forlorn.
(It looked as though it couldn’t accept its own fate.) …I’m sorry. You were a good tuna mayo.
Yeoni bought another one. This time, it didn’t fall. But the first bite set their mouth on fire. Spicy pork. The wrapper had clearly said tuna mayo.
Seriously? Even the rice triangles are lying to me now?
The rice triangle said nothing. Naturally. It was a rice triangle.
Tuna mayo on the outside, spicy pork on the inside. Isn’t that false advertising? I’m filing a consumer complaint. I mean it.
Up to that point, it had been funny. The sort of thing a friend would laugh off with, “What is going on with you today?”
But a few days later—it stopped being funny.

A part-time job interview was canceled that very day. An assignment file became corrupted just before submission. A parcel went to the wrong building. A café coupon had expired yesterday, discovered only at the counter.
An important message came back as failed to send. Apologies always arrived a moment too late, and words meant to help somehow came out wrong.
Once, three dots flickered in a chat window. Something was about to arrive—then quietly vanished.
Yeoni stared for a long time at the space where those three dots had been, then turned the phone face down.

The room’s darkness settled softly over the overturned phone. Yeoni pulled the blanket up to their nose. It was one of those nights when no one was to blame, yet everything made you feel sorry. There had been more and more nights like that.
…Why does everything keep going wrong? Did I do something?

Small misfortunes gnawed a little more out of each day. At first, Yeoni had laughed them off as coincidences. But when coincidences pile up for days, the back of your neck grows cold, as if someone is standing behind you. Days begun with a joke had become days spent looking for excuses.
Still, Yeoni didn’t want to believe in fate. It was far too convenient a word.
If things fail, it’s fate. If you break up, it wasn’t meant to be. If you’re late, the time wasn’t right… Those sayings always leave me stuck in the same place.
They made everything easier to explain. They did nothing to make it easier to bear.
That night, Yeoni peeled off the wet socks, tossed them aside, and collapsed onto the bed. Enough thinking about today.
Today was… one for the history books.
Battery: 4 percent. Yeoni reached for the charger—and the screen lit up on its own.
…What?
In the middle of the home screen sat an unfamiliar app. A black night sky. A doorway traced in moonlight. One tiny star. And two words.
〈  Code Destiny  〉
Did I… install this?
No memory of it. Yeoni pressed and held the app to delete it. The screen answered.

[ This app cannot be deleted. ]
[ This app is connected to destiny. ]
Apps these days have some serious nerve.
I never paid for it, but apparently there are no refunds. No, forget refunds—I can’t even delete it. Five stars for sheer audacity.
Yeoni checked Settings. It wasn’t in the app list or the storage menu. But there it was on the home screen, utterly at ease. As though that spot had always belonged to it.
Then a notification appeared.

[ User fortune damage: 87% ]
[ Luck leak detected · Bond code partially corrupted · Abnormal wealth code outflow ]
[ User: Yeoni ]  [ Age: 23 ]  [ Day Master candidate: 乙 ]  [ Day Pillar code: 乙亥 ]
How… how do you know my name and age?
[ The universe has always known. ]
That makes it even creepier!
Enough. Where’s customer support? Put me through to a person. Right now.

[ Customer support: The universe ]
[ Agents: None · Your place in the queue: ∞ ]
Yeoni tossed the phone onto the pillow. It bounced a couple of times, then lit up again.
[ Begin destiny restoration? ]     [ YES ]     [ Later ]
Naturally, Yeoni tapped [Later]. The screen changed.
[ There is no later. ]
…Then why did you ask?
[ YES ]     [ YES ]
That isn’t a choice. That’s a kidnapping notice.

[ Terms of Service, Article 1 ]
[ By being born, the user has already agreed to all provisions. ]
A tarot card rose above the screen. Against black, a door made of moonlight. A small flower before it. At the bottom—[ THE DOOR ].
Is that… even a tarot card?
At that moment, the door in the card opened. Creeeeak—the sound came from the room, not the phone.
A real moonlit door stood in the air at the foot of the bed. Beyond its narrow opening, an unfamiliar night sky swirled.
This is… still my room, right?

Instead of an answer, cards poured through the doorway. The Star, the Moon, the Sun, the Wheel of Fortune. The assignment on the desk, the inside-out umbrella, even the half-eaten cup noodles began circling the room.
My assignment, my umbrella, my noodles—…Actually, forget the noodles!
[ Tarot gate open ]  [ Connecting to the fortune world ]  [ River of Saju coordinates confirmed ]
Close it. I said close it! A river? This is a studio apartment!
[ Converting initial avatar ]
Light burst from inside the doorway. Yeoni clung to the headboard until the very end. The headboard, unfortunately, was less loyal than expected. Snap.
Traitor!
And just like that—Yeoni was sucked through the tarot gate.
Beyond the door lay endless night. Night above, night below. Constellations flowed like a river, and countless tarot cards circled Yeoni, whispering. Choice. Descent. Beginning. Transformation.
[ Destiny code connection complete ]  [ Entering the damaged fortune world. ]
I never agreed to—
